questions.question:
**Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error.**

The Hindi question paper was extremely tougher for 7th grade students.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is 'tougher'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• The error lies in** 'tougher' **part of the sentence. 
 
• Here, extremely is the adverb form of the adjective extreme which means of the highest degree or intensity.
 
• So, instead of 'tougher' we will use 'tough' after extremely.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **option 1.**

**Correct Sentence**: *The Hindi question paper was **extremely tough **for 7th-grade students.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**However**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses the shift in children's entertainment from storybooks to digital media.
 
• The word "However" is used to introduce a contrast, which fits well as the sentence contrasts the past with the present.
 
• "**However**" fits well as it indicates a change or difference in the scenario being described.
 
• Other options ("**While**", "**Though**", "**In spite**") do not fit the context of contrasting past and present habits as clearly.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *There was a time when storybooks were the only (1) ______ of entertainment for children. A decade or two ago, kids (2) ______ their time reading stories and role playing (3) ______ favourite characters from the stories. **However*__*, times have changed now – in the age of the internet, kids spend (5) ______ of their time playing games on smartphones or watching cartoons or videos on YouTube.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• While (हालाँकि): "While" suggests two things happening simultaneously, which doesn't fit the context of contrasting the past and present habits.
 
• Though (यद्यपि): "Though" can introduce a contrast, but it's usually used where a follow-up clause negates or downplays the previous fact.
 
• In spite (इसके बावजूद): "In spite" is used for contrast but indicates overcoming an obstacle, which doesn't fit the context as clearly here.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Mother beat Jenny / by a stick / for going out / without permission.
questions.solution:
The erroneous segment is** 'by a stick'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is** grammatically incorrect.**
 
• The error lies in** part B** of the sentence.
 
• Here **stick** is an inanimate subject and the preposition** 'with'** is used instead of '**by'** in the case of an inanimate subject.
 
• Here, instead of **'by a stick'** we will use 'with a stick' for making this given sentence **error-free.**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **option 3.**

**​Correct Sentence: **Mother beat Jenny with a stick for going out without permission. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• We use** Preposition 'By' for an agent **and while **using some instrument/ equipment, preposition ‘ with' is used**.

 
 
• ***Example: **He was beaten **with **a stick.*
